conclusion: A committed MessageType 18 branch and passing policy harness prove that the handler and fail-closed rules exist, but they do not prove a positive Unix-socket type-18 route. The retained live probe proves only canonical unsupported-capability negotiation and baseline reconnect while bit 8 remains clear.
decision: Track handler_source_present, route_policy_harness, live_handshake_canonical_unsupported, and daemon_socket_route as separate claims. Keep capability bit 8 unadvertised until a live negotiated client sends type 18 and completes every owner-bound stage without relying on the policy harness as socket evidence.
invalidated_assumptions: A source-level dispatch branch automatically proves that production capability negotiation can reach it.
A policy harness that encodes a canonical type-19 failure is equivalent to a raw type-18 request over the live Unix socket.
A successful baseline reconnect after generic-capability rejection permits capability bit 8 to be advertised.
observation: CP24 commits an owner-bound generic session, type-18 handler branch, type-19 outbound plumbing, and a route-policy harness. The live runtime-to-gem5 endpoint test requests generic capability, receives canonical UnsupportedCapability because bit 8 is absent, reconnects with baseline capabilities, and sends no MessageType 18 frame.
question_or_symptom: Which CP24 results demonstrate real daemon reachability, and which still stop short of a positive generic-dispatch socket route?
